To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CZT detectors grown by the MHB process can be used for a broad range of applications, that the choice of the anode material can have an impact on the detector performance, that the best results can be achieved with low-work-function materials, and that temperature dependent measurements can provide important information on detector parameters.

the anode work-function is important for the performance of MHB CZT detectors and that the energy resolution deteriorates at lower temperature, but this effect is reversible by increasing the bias voltage.
the best performance of CZT detectors with 8 mm pixel pitch was achieved with low-work-function anodes (In or Ti) and the energy resolution is temperature dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a systematic investigation of the influence of the anode contact on the performance of MHB CZT detectors.
the optimization of CZT detectors for applications in medical imaging and nuclear security.
the development of CZT detectors for medical applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the detector performance is not only determined by the work-function of the anode material, but it is also influenced by the temperature.
low-work-function materials on both cathode and anode are beneficial for the performance of pixelated CZTDetectors.
the best performance of the detectors is achieved with Indium or Titanium as anode material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the detector material grown with the MHB process is very promising for a wide range of applications, in particular, for medical imaging.
the MHB method is an inexpensive method to produce CZT crystals, and that it is possible to achieve good detector performance by optimizing the anode and cathode materials.
the use of low-work-function anode materials improves the energy resolution and that the use of high-work-function cathode materials reduces the leakage current.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anode material has a significant influence on the performance of CZT pixelated detectors.
CZT crystals with a large pixel pitch can be grown with the MHB method and that they can be processed to achieve a good energy resolution.
CZT grown with the modified Bridgman method can achieve excellent performance, which is comparable to that achieved with detectors made with material grown by the conventional HPB method.
